# Assembly Line Balancer: fewest stations at takt, or shortest cycle on a set number of stations

> Free tool for manufacturing, industrial and lean engineers, plant managers and students: type tasks, times and direct predecessors, give a cycle time (takt, or available time and demand) or a number of stations, and get the fewest stations (SALBP-1) or the shortest cycle (SALBP-2) by an exact branch, bound and remember search that says when it has proved the answer optimal and otherwise gives the proved bound. Line efficiency, balance delay, smoothness index, idle time and a station load chart. On Scholl's 269 SALBP-1 benchmark problems it matched the published optimum on 258 of 269 at 4 seconds each (bench/salbp1.md). Nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are planning estimates, not engineering advice; zoning, ergonomics, tooling, variation and mixed models are not modelled.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/assembly-line-balancer/): task table (or CSV, JSON, Scholl .IN2 file) in; stations, cycle time, efficiency, idle, a station chart and a CSV of the balance out.
- [How it works](https://marisstella.app/assembly-line-balancer/how-it-works.html): lower bounds, priority rules (ranked positional weight and three others, forwards and backwards), the exact search, and the full benchmark results.

## How to use the engine

- `engine.mjs` exports `minimizeStations({tasks, cycleTime}, {ms, nodes})` (stationCount, lowerBound, optimal, stations[{station, tasks, load, idle}], efficiency, balanceDelay, smoothnessIndex, assignment), `minimizeCycleTime({tasks}, stations, limits)`, `taktTime(available, demand)`, `checkBalance(problem, assignment, cycleTime)`, `parseTaskTable(text)`, `parseIn2(text)`, `formatTaskTable(problem)`, `EXAMPLE` (Jackson 1956). A task is `{id, time, predecessors: [ids], name?}`.
- `cli.mjs`: `node cli.mjs tasks.csv --cycle 60`, `--stations 8`, `--takt 27000,450`, `--json`, `--ms 4000`.
